verbatim_phrase: drawing the bow without exerting pressure on the stick
quote: one must practise creating the sound that can be made when one draws the bow without exerting pressure on the stick

verbatim_phrase: flat hair on the down bow to get a thicker tone
quote: Try using a flat hair on the down bow to get a thicker tone. Draw with the fingers working closely together and the palm facing out.

verbatim_phrase: on the up bow, the stick is turned slightly and played at an angle
quote: On the up bow, the stick is turned slightly and played at an angle.

verbatim_phrase: seamless bow changes
quote: An occasional wrap on the wrist with a yardstick kept my wrist down and flexible so that my fingers could affect seamless bow changes.

verbatim_phrase: drawing the bow from frog to tip on open strings
quote: For six months I had lessons on open strings, drawing the bow from frog to tip.

verbatim_phrase: amount of pressure applied must be proportionate to your bow speed
quote: The amount of pressure applied must be proportionate to your bow speed – herein lies the secret to creating a quality tone rather than a forced tone.

verbatim_phrase: sustain vibrance from note to note, finger to finger and position to position
quote: he could sustain his vibrance from note to note, finger to finger and position to position and there was never a "wasted", dead note in his tonal lexicon

verbatim_phrase: laying the bow lightly upon the strings at the first contact
quote: This depends on laying the bow lightly upon the strings at the first contact, and on gently pressing it afterwards

verbatim_phrase: weight of the bow carried by two middle fingers and thumb, not forefinger
quote: they employ the forefinger for holding, incidentally, carrying, the weight of the bow. This should be chiefly done by the two middle fingers and the thumb.

verbatim_phrase: subtleties of angle, pressure and placement between fingerboard and bridge
quote: In Mozart and Beethoven he was eminently straightforward, inflecting his bowing with myriad subtleties of angle, pressure and placement between fingerboard and bridge.

verbatim_phrase: liquidity of position-changes
quote: His fingers appeared to caress the fingerboard with the minimum of perceived effort and height, and the liquidity of his position-changes made the potentially hazardous appear graceful.

verbatim_phrase: relaxed bow hold that never stiffened even when playing staccato or marcato
quote: his supremely relaxed bow hold, which never appeared to stiffen even when playing staccato or marcato

verbatim_phrase: little finger raised through most of the stroke, contacting stick to counterbalance bow change
quote: The little finger was raised through most of the stroke, only coming into contact with the stick as the heel approached and departed the violin so as to counterbalance each bow change

verbatim_phrase: unusually flexible index finger
quote: a technique that was facilitated by an unusually flexible index finger

verbatim_phrase: medium–fast, full bow strokes delivering a full-throated sound
quote: His medium–fast, full bow strokes delivered a full-throated sound midway between Milstein's satin purity and Stern's galvanising strength.

verbatim_phrase: shift like a train journey — gather, disembark, without haste
quote: the motion "like a train journey from A to B: before arriving at B, one gathers together one's things, gets up and disembarks, but without haste"

verbatim_phrase: vibrato relaxes at the end of the phrase
quote: vibrato should "support the line or phrase, so that at the end of the phrase, the vibrato relaxes."

verbatim_phrase: keep left wrist straight, don't let violin neck rest on palm or wrist
quote: Keep your wrist straight. Don't let the violin neck rest on your palm or wrist. This incorrect hand position will make it impossible to do vibrato on the violin

verbatim_phrase: least amount of pressure possible to press the string down
quote: Use the Least Amount of Pressure Possible to Press the String Down

verbatim_phrase: slide one finger up and down the fingerboard bringing thumb with you
quote: Put one finger down on the string and slide it up and down the violin (bringing your thumb with you). Do this with all fingers on all strings.

verbatim_phrase: relax knuckle closest to fingernail with give in it for vibrato
quote: The knuckle closest to the fingernail must be relaxed and have some "give" in it for vibrato.

verbatim_phrase: detaché — separate strokes with seamless bow change
quote: Detaché is a versatile technique found in almost every violin repertoire. It involves separate strokes, down and up, with a seamless bow change.

verbatim_phrase: detaché collé — slow-motion spiccato lifting the bow at the changes
quote: try detaché collé, a slow-motion spiccato where you lift the bow at the changes.

verbatim_phrase: detaché porté — emphasize start of each stroke with higher bow speed but no pressure accents
quote: detaché porté, where you emphasize the start of each stroke with higher bow speed but without pressure accents

verbatim_phrase: martelé — each note begins with distinct accent, slight pause between notes
quote: With martelé, each note begins with a distinct accent, and there's a slight pause between the notes.

verbatim_phrase: apply weight of arm through index finger into the bow, releasing at start of each stroke
quote: Apply the weight of your arm through your index finger into the bow, releasing it at the start of each stroke.

verbatim_phrase: martelé lancé — longer stroke with higher bow speed and firm accents
quote: martelé lancé, a longer stroke with higher bow speed and firm accents

verbatim_phrase: spiccato — harness natural bounce of the bow with short strokes, wrist and fingers
quote: Spiccato is all about harnessing the natural bounce of the bow. The strokes are short, and your wrist and fingers make smooth movements. Avoid using your entire arm for spiccato

verbatim_phrase: sautillé — faster tempo played higher on the bow
quote: Take it up a notch with sautillé, a faster tempo played higher on the bow.

verbatim_phrase: flying spiccato — several notes on one stroke, almost vertically jumping from the string
quote: flying spiccato, where you play several notes on one stroke, almost vertically jumping from the string

verbatim_phrase: tremolo — short bow strokes at the tip
quote: With short bow strokes at the tip, Tremolo adds a shimmering effect.

verbatim_phrase: col legno — flip the bow upside down, play with the wood against the strings
quote: Col legno flips the bow upside down, letting you play with the wood against the strings for a unique timbre.

verbatim_phrase: sul ponticello — near the bridge
quote: Sul punticello, near the bridge, conjures a classy and refined sound

verbatim_phrase: sul tasto — near or above the fingerboard
quote: sul tasto, near or above the fingerboard, delivers a soft and ethereal tone

verbatim_phrase: flautato — high-speed bowing with little pressure, whistling transparent sound
quote: flautato, a high-speed bowing technique with little pressure that creates a whistling, transparent sound

verbatim_phrase: keep elbow at right angle when changing strings
quote: Maintain this squared position as you play, ensuring your arm retains the right angle when changing strings.

verbatim_phrase: keep the bow flat on the strings
quote: beginners and intermediate players should focus on keeping the bow flat on the strings for better control and depth of sound

verbatim_phrase: shift with arm, hand and fingers working as a team
quote: Have the Arm hand and fingers work as a team. Don't just shift up with the finger and leave everone else behind.

verbatim_phrase: bring left elbow under the instrument for higher positions
quote: Let your elbow help you maneuver around to the higher positions. Bring it under the instrument to have easier access to higher positions

verbatim_phrase: hear the new pitch in your head before shifting to it
quote: Always HEAR the new pitch in your head before shifting to it. You will seriously be surprised at how quickly this improves your intonation accuracy in shifting.

verbatim_phrase: practice shifts fast even in slow pieces to avoid slides
quote: just because the piece may be slow you still need to get to the new position just as cleanly without slides in most cases so the shift needs to be practiced fast

verbatim_phrase: practice shifting down the instrument as much as up
quote: Practice Shifting down the instrument as much as up. So much time is spent on shifting up.

verbatim_phrase: press index finger down to create initial sound and release once bow starts to travel
quote: "catch and release"—instilled in him by his mentor Ivan Galamian—in which he presses the index finger down to create an initial sound and releases the pressure once the bow starts to travel

verbatim_phrase: not mashing the string past where the note is clear (throws pitch sharp)
quote: a player might tend to mash the string down past where the note is already clear, which doesn't help the sound—it actually throws the pitch sharp and deadens your sensitivity

verbatim_phrase: move thumb forward before using fourth finger for clean balanced finger swing
quote: violinists need to move their thumb forward before using the fourth finger to enable a clean, balanced finger swing

verbatim_phrase: arm suspended above the string, bow connects without crushing as it swings in an arc
quote: the arm should be supported and suspended just above the string, allowing the bow to connect without crushing as it swings in an arc

verbatim_phrase: fingers descend in a natural arc from a relaxing base knuckle, rebound on release
quote: fingers should descend in a natural arc from a relaxing base knuckle, aiming to crisply clear the note's threshold with a sense of rebound on release

verbatim_phrase: fingers binary 'down' or 'not down', not gradual
quote: Even when playing slowly, there isn't a gradual element in the fingers—it's a binary 'down' or 'not down.'

verbatim_phrase: use sympathetic vibrations (D on A string ringing open D) as tuning fork
quote: sympathetic vibrations—like a D on the A string making the open D ring—are so useful. Those little resonances act as a kind of tuning fork

verbatim_phrase: sense of pulse and rhythm — no wrong notes in rests
quote: Crucial skills include a sense of pulse and rhythm (no one likes to let out a stonking wrong note in a rest)

verbatim_phrase: bow choreography — bow in same direction as everyone else's
quote: bow choreography (if your bow is in the same direction as everyone else's, who's to be any the wiser?)

verbatim_phrase: wild, free lines in waves from bottom of violin's spectrum to quarter inch from top of fingerboard
quote: I have these wild, free lines travelling in waves from the bottom of the violin's spectrum to a quarter of an inch from the top of the fingerboard and back down

verbatim_phrase: passages that may not even be technically possible for many players

verbatim_phrase: restless arpeggios that echo Berg and Ligeti's violin concertos

verbatim_phrase: sustained tone production
quote: this movement becomes a foundational study in sustained tone production, bow control across long phrases, expressive phrasing without excess tension

verbatim_phrase: bow control across long phrases
quote: sustained tone production, bow control across long phrases, expressive phrasing without excess tension, and musical clarity within a slow tempo

verbatim_phrase: elaborate carefully notated ornamentation giving a free, improvisatory impression
quote: Bach's elaborate ornamentation in the G minor Adagio makes a fitting opening... his ornamentation is carefully notated, though the Adagio gives a free, improvisatory impression

quote: the chord C/A/F# is awkward on the violin for the left hand. It also requires a shift up the neck

verbatim_phrase: arpeggiating across all the strings requiring a large movement with the bowing arm
quote: a louder, arpeggiating across all the strings, and requiring a large movement with the bowing arm

quote: measure 9 features "a simple octave double stop on the two inner strings"

verbatim_phrase: digital and rhythmic dexterity and preciseness of pitch in the multiple stoppings

verbatim_phrase: inner-ear sensitivity to implied polyphonic and harmonic textures
quote: the keenest musical insights and inner-ear sensitivity to implied polyphonic and harmonic textures

verbatim_phrase: multi-stopping and chords are challenging to say the least
quote: The multi-stopping and chords are challenging to say the least. I must study Heifetz's masterclass

verbatim_phrase: arpeggios and scale passages juxtaposed

verbatim_phrase: richly chordal passages in the Sarabanda
quote: The Sarabanda, by contrast, with its richly chordal passages gives the impression, to some extent illusory, of greater complexity.

verbatim_phrase: kaleidoscope of technical devices pushing the boundaries of the baroque violinist's art
quote: a kaleidoscope of technical devices both pushing the boundaries of, and summarizing, we might say, the baroque violinist's art

verbatim_phrase: quadruple-stop chordal texture
quote: the amount of sound issuing from the instrument expands dramatically from single notes to quadruple-stop chordal texture

verbatim_phrase: implied part-writing spinning two- and three-voice textures at dazzling speed
quote: the Allegro assai finale demonstrates implied part-writing spinning two- and three-voice textures at dazzling speed

verbatim_phrase: substantial contrapuntal challenges and intimidating technical requirements
quote: The movement presents substantial contrapuntal challenges and intimidating technical requirements for performers.

quote: this is the longest and most complex of the fugues in the Sei Solo—it is technically extremely demanding, with polyphony full of (arpeggiated) 3- and 4-stop chords.

verbatim_phrase: maintaining sound and sonority at the fast pace

verbatim_phrase: densely worked theme almost ever present and discernible throughout

quote: The Siciliana, in which three voices are sustained, has something of the character of a trio sonata movement.

verbatim_phrase: digital and rhythmic dexterity and preciseness of pitch in the multiple stoppings
quote: They demand not only unfaltering facility in matters of digital and rhythmic dexterity and preciseness of pitch, particularly in the multiple stoppings

quote: a dashing, bravura Preludio whose almost unbroken pattern of semiquavers, together with passages of 'bariolage'

quote: Block fingerings are recommended—for example, using one finger to hold consecutive notes across strings. This reduces unnecessary motion.

quote: Separate bows to ensure open string resonance
